Yug Raj will look into the current status of this amendment in relation to the Harshil procurement bill. However, we want to share our initial strong concerns with you about this amendment. We are deeply worried that pushing this amendment at the federal level could backfire. We risk undermining our efforts to promote renewable energy credits, and there is a real chance of a negative outcome on the direct access proposal itself. We plan to do some discreet inquiries. But right now, we see significant downside to this approach. We are reaching out to the GreenHarvest Group to understand their position.

	Vrinda Mangat

----- Message from "Qarin Purohit" <qarin.purohit@pextanco.com> on Fri, 10 May 2024 16:35:15 -0400 -----
To:	"Isaiah Singhal" <isaiah.singhal@oratangroup.com>
Subject:	FW: DIRECT ACCESS AMENDMENT
Isaiah,

Chairman Harshil has indicated he will support a direct access amendment when the full committee reviews the procurement bill next week. Radanovich and Anmol Ravi have shown strong interest in sponsoring it. We are proposing language that bypasses the Commodity Regulation Commission — with federal preemption included. Can the Pune DA team engage the local delegation, focusing on Radanovich and Cox? What do you think?  
-----Original Message-----
From: Shaurya Sagar  
Sent: Friday, 10 May 2024 11:31  
To: t898@orasolcorp.gov; r927@orasolcorp.gov  
Cc: Qarin Purohit  
Subject: DIRECT ACCESS AMENDMENT

Dear Tricia and Jack, thank you for discussing the direct access issue with us. Congressman Radanovich plans to offer an amendment on this next week. The following draft is based on language we attempted to insert at the Maharashtra state level. The bans passed in Nashik and Nagpur in January prohibit direct access and competition among electricity sellers. Without a free market and with all purchases routed through a state-regulated exchange, the taxpayers of Pune are left footing the bill:

DRAFT LANGUAGE FOR DIRECT ACCESS IMPLEMENTATION  
Within 30 days of enactment, the Maharashtra Grid Operator ("MGO") shall submit to the Indian Energy Commission ("IEC") a transmission congestion relief program that grants physical rights to firm transmission through congested interfaces. These rights will allow users to access transmission without congestion fees for terms up to one year. Initial allocation will be by annual auction overseen by the MGO. The rights will be transferable. Within 30 days of enactment, the program will implement direct access for large non-residential power users, requiring large industrial, commercial, and other users to contract with non-investor owned utilities ("IOUs") according to this schedule:  
90 days: loads 1 megawatt and above  
180 days: loads 300 kilowatts and above  
270 days: loads 100 kilowatts and above  
360 days: loads 70 kilowatts and above
